answer: A garden economy can resist Sybils by making influence grow slowly, like plants, not appear on demand. Each newcomer gets one small plot and a single quill key signing every contribution. Tending it—watering shared tasks, weeding bad data, helping neighbours—earns growth; neglect makes it wither. A velvet gate admits only mature plots to paid work, so influence cannot be bought or cloned instantly. An attacker wanting a thousand voices must tend a thousand plots for weeks, paying real time and attention, while thriving honest gardeners stay cheap to verify and hard to imitate at scale.
